title: Sundance Breakout ‘Thelma’ Set for Mandarin Remake by Stars Collective, Titled ‘Grandma, Please’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Stars Collective has acquired the Mandarin-language remake rights to “Thelma,” the 2024 Sundance Film Festival breakout that became Magnolia Picture
body:
Stars Collective has acquired the Mandarin-language remake rights to “Thelma,” the 2024 Sundance Film Festival breakout that became Magnolia Pictures’ highest-grossing narrative feature, and is developing an adaptation titled “Grandma, Please.”

	In “Grandma, Please,” an 80-year-old grandmother is swindled out of her life savings by a scammer who uses AI to clone her late husband’s voice. Rather than involve the police or worry her children, she decides to track down the culprit herself – a search that reunites her with an old flame from 60 years earlier, once a basketball team captain and now a resident of a care home. Their journey together turns into a road trip blending comedy with more emotional beats.
	

	The original “Thelma,” written and directed by Josh Margolin and produced by Zurich Avenue and Bandwagon, starred a then-93-year-old June Squibb in the title role, with Parker Posey as her uptight daughter and Fred Hechinger as her grandson. The film was released theatrically in the U.S. by Magnolia Pictures.


	Peter Luo, known for “Malignant,” “Scary Stories to Tell in the Dark” and “Crazy Rich Asians,” is writing the adapted screenplay and producing alongside Stars Collective Co-CEO Nancy Xu and Wayne Wei Jiang, whose credits include “The Meg.” Luo and Xu most recently executive produced “The Rip,” starring Matt Damon and Ben Affleck, which reached No. 1 on Netflix’s global film chart.

	Xu negotiated the deal with Team Thelma LLC, which produced and owns the original film and controls its remake rights. Production on “Grandma, Please” is expected to begin in the second half of 2027.
	

	“‘Thelma’ may have seemed like an unlikely action-comedy hit, but the movie really played intergenerationally and the audience reflected this,” Luo said. “The story’s appeal extends beyond seniors, and we love the message the film sends – at any age, you can be the lead in your own life. We have an exciting vision for this reimagining and are excited to share it.”

	Xu said senior-led stories such as “Thelma” and “How to Make Millions Before Grandma Dies” have been driving global box office surprises, and this reimagining aims to ride that same wave. “‘Grandma, Please’ offers a fun genre premise with real social relevance beneath the comedy, and we feel this will translate to box office popularity,” Xu added.

	Founded in 2020 by Luo, Stars Collective is a global intellectual property company with operations in Los Angeles, China and Japan. The company has more than 60 original IPs in development across film, animation, games, consumer products and immersive experiences.

	Recent Stars Collective productions include “The Monkey” and “PLayland.” The company holds a 25-year exclusive merchandising license for “The Garfield Movie” in Greater China, covering all categories except theme park and stage rights. Stars Collective also optioned the film rights to the nonfiction book “Fortunate Sons: The 120 Chinese Boys Who Came to America, Went to School, and Revolutionized an Ancient Civilization,” and is developing a movie adaptation with Academy Award winner Donna Gigliotti.

	Stars Collective is also building a studio focused on generative technology that will bring Hollywood filmmakers together with AI tools.

schema.headline: Sundance Breakout ‘Thelma’ Set for Mandarin Remake by Stars Collective, Titled ‘Grandma, Please’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Continue Tussle Atop U.K., Ireland Box Office
description: Sony’s superhero tentpole “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” dominated the U.K. and Ireland box office for a third consecutive weekend, adding £6.1 million
body:
Sony’s superhero tentpole “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” dominated the U.K. and Ireland box office for a third consecutive weekend, adding £6.1 million ($8.3 million), elevating its running total to $106.5 million after 20 days of release.

	Universal’s epic “The Odyssey” held onto second place in its fifth frame. Directed by Christopher Nolan, the wide release collected $5 million, driving its cume to $93.4 million. 


	Warner Bros.’ “The End of Oak Street,” starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor, arrived in third place with an opening weekend of $2.8 million. Trafalgar Releasing claimed fourth spot with the wide event cinema launch of music doc “Katseye: Wild Hearts,” which banked $981,457 in its debut frame.
	

	Paramount’s “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” moved to fifth position in its second weekend, adding £$940,306 for a cumulative total of $4.3 million. Disney took sixth place with “Toy Story 5,” which added £$714,080 in its ninth frame to lift its running total to $74.7 million. 

	Universal’s “Minions & Monsters” followed in seventh position in its seventh week, generating $546,233 to push its cume to $23.2 million. A24 secured eighth place with the debut of Matt Johnson’s Anthony Bourdain film “Tony,” starring Dominic Sessa and Antonio Banderas, taking $544,524.

	Disney’s live-action “Moana” took ninth spot in its sixth week of release, collecting $441,419 to raise its running total to $17.2 million. TGS Cinemas Limited rounded out the top 10 with the launch of Indian drama “Vishwanath & Sons,” which generated an opening frame of $378,751.
	

	Looking ahead to the upcoming theatrical frame, rollouts began with Source Entertainment releasing Chris Atkins’ music documentary “James: Getting Away with It” across more than 100 locations.

	Wide commercial openings across 300+ locations include horror sequel “Insidious: Out of the Further,” distributed by Sony, Studiocanal’s Jason Statham vehicle “Mutiny,” and Black Bear’s comedy “Spa Weekend.” 

	Debuts also include Altitude’s long-awaited “Coyote vs. Acme,” Mubi’s “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” Icon’s “& Sons,” Universal’s “Stop! That! Train!,” and Vue Lumiere’s “David.” 

	Repertory screenings feature Park Circus re-releasing the 30th anniversary restoration of Danny Boyle’s “Trainspotting” alongside Aardman’s animated comedy “Early Man.” Anime Ltd is re-releasing a restored version of Miyazaki Hayao’s 1989 masterpiece “Kiki’s Delivery Service.”

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Continue Tussle Atop U.K., Ireland Box Office

title: Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Starts Shooting in December
description:
Vin Diesel says filming for “Fast Forever” has a start date.

	“We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio,” D
body:
Vin Diesel says filming for “Fast Forever” has a start date.

	“We start shooting in December, if I can make good on the request from the studio,” Diesel told Variety Monday night at the 25th anniversary screening of “The Fast and the Furious.” “I’m in a good place, though. I had to go through four sets of writers, four years of development, to get to something that I felt would be worthy of a finale. And when I read the script a couple of weeks ago, [I cried].”
	

	Inside the screening, Diesel addressed the audience before the lights dimmed and shared more details about how the “Fast Forever” script brought him to tears.


	“I’m going to tell you something personal,” he said. “It was after four different writers, four years of development, and after I read the script, halfway through, one tear. By the end of the script that we crafted and worked so hard to make right for you after four years, I was crying. I couldn’t hold it back, and I had to tell everyone. And my sister said, ‘No more crying, bro.’ So I just want to say that sometimes, even the toughest guys in the world need to cry.”


	“Fast Forever,” the 11th and final mainline film in the series, hits theaters on March 17, 2028. “Fast & Furious” is Universal’s longest-running franchise and its most profitable, with a combined worldwide gross of $7.3 billion.

	While Diesel is all in on the latest “Fast Forever” draft, director Louis Leterrier recently told Polygon that he’s yet to read the script.
	

	“I’d love to tell you the full truth, but I can’t,” Leterrier said. “There will be an ending, and it’s great. I was very, very lucky to be part of the franchise, and I love Vin and I love Universal. They’re great to work with. So yeah. We’ll see, hopefully.”

schema.headline: Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Starts Shooting in December

title: Rosie O’Donnell Shines in ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hosting Debut, Attacks ‘Mango Mussolini’ Trump and Gives Moving Hayden Panettiere Tribute
description: When Jimmy Kimmel announced that Rosie O’Donnell would be filling in as a week-long guest host of “Jimmy Kimmel Live” during his summer vacation, he
body:
When Jimmy Kimmel announced that Rosie O’Donnell would be filling in as a week-long guest host of “Jimmy Kimmel Live” during his summer vacation, he teased it would be “a special treat” for Donald Trump, who’s harbored a 20-year-long vendetta against the comic for her mocking his bankruptcies on “The View” back in 2006.

	O’Donnell told Variety she was “surprised” by the guest-hosting offer from Kimmel, given the pair’s “adversarial relationship” and the fact that she’d never even been asked on as a guest, but she was “thankful” and accepted nevertheless, owing in large part to her support of Kimmel during Trump’s relentless campaign to get his late-night show canceled over jokes he didn’t like.
	

	“I support [Kimmel] in what he’s doing with the First Amendment, and our ability as entertainers and citizens to speak out against our government that’s enshrined in the Founding Fathers’ writings about our government, so I think he’s fantastic,” O’Donnell said. “And I wish that Stephen Colbert had the same kind of support when it happened to him, because he shouldn’t be gone either.”

	On Monday night, O’Donnell kicked off her “Jimmy Kimmel Live” hosting duties by strutting out onstage in a bright pink suit adorned with flowers — to lengthy applause and chants of “RO-SIE! RO-SIE!” — before declaring, “If you thought the president hated ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ when it was hosted by Jimmy Kimmel? Buckle up, people! Buckle up.”



	The former host of “The Rosie O’Donnell Show” and “The View” continued taking shots at her thin-skinned nemesis during her monologue, joking, “I’ve been living in Ireland for the past two years because of ‘Mango Mussolini.’ I read that Project 2025 and said, ‘Gotta get myself out of here!’ and I decided to go to Ireland where people are driven to drink regardless of who’s running their country.”
	

	At one point during her monologue, she turned to the camera and addressed Trump, saying, “Hi! I know you’re watching!”

	O’Donnell seemed cool and collected at the helm of a late-night show after decades away from TV hosting, regaling the audience with jokes about her time living in Ireland, including the disarming kindness of strangers (compared to New York City), their enthusiastic drinking and trying to ask out her (straight) pharmacist, and getting along famously with her guests, including “Ted Lasso” star Hannah Waddingham, who announced herself as a huge Rosie fan (“I can’t believe I’m talking to Rosie O’Donnell… I’m losing my mind!” she exclaimed), and “Schmigadoon!’s” Ana Gasteyer.

	Between guests, O’Donnell choked up while giving a moving tribute to the late Hayden Panettiere, who tragically passed away on Sunday at the age of 36. Panettiere had been a favorite guest of “The Rosie O’Donnell Show” as a child actress.

	“I’m just heartbroken over the passing of Hayden Panettiere last night. She was on my show many times as a little girl, and I got to know her as a grown woman,” offered O’Donnell. “And she was so brave talking about mental health before people were really ready to hear about it, and very sad. My love to her family and friends, and she will be missed. Godspeed, Hayden.”

	Overall, O’Donnell seemed to acquit herself well as a late-night host. Cue the angry Trump posts.

schema.headline: Rosie O’Donnell Shines in ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Hosting Debut, Attacks ‘Mango Mussolini’ Trump and Gives Moving Hayden Panettiere Tribute

title: Jeanie Buss Seeks to Contest Sale of Los Angeles Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner: Report
description: Jeanie Buss, the Los Angeles Lakers owner who has been the face of the team since the death of her father Jerry Buss in 2013, is reportedly contesti
body:
Jeanie Buss, the Los Angeles Lakers owner who has been the face of the team since the death of her father Jerry Buss in 2013, is reportedly contesting the plan approved by her siblings to sell the family’s remaining 18% stake in the storied NBA franchise to investors Bob Iger and Josh Kushner.

	ESPN and numerous outlets reported Monday that Buss is challenging her siblings’ right to approve the sale of the team to the former Disney CEO and Kushner, an investor who founded Thrive Capital in 2010 at age 24.
	

	Jeanie Buss and her five siblings — Jesse, Jim, Johnny, Janie and Joey — have had complicated legal maneuvering around the management of the team. In 2017, following a litigation process, Jeanie was designated the controlling owner of the team through 2030. Jeanie Buss’ attorneys indicated that she asserts that she has the right to approve any sale of the team. Iger reportedly had met with Jeanie and vowed to honor the agreement she had with Mark Walter to remain at the helm through 2030.


	Walter, the CEO of Guggenheim Partners, acquired the Lakers from the Buss family in June 2025. The deal was finalized in October 2025, when the NBA distributed a photo of Walter sitting next to a smiling Jeanie Buss.

	A representative for Iger and Kushner did not immediately respond to a request for comment late Monday.

	Per ESPN, Jeanie Buss’ lawyer, Adam Streisand, has sent correspondence to the five Buss siblings who voted to sell that “a court had ruled in 2017 that no sale could be “effectuated without approval by the co-trustees, i.e. Jeanie, Janie and Joey Buss,” as reported by ESPN’s Ramona Shelburne.
	

	Iger and Kushner surprised the industry and the sports world on Aug. 12 with their deal to acquire the Lakers from Walter for $12.5 billion — a premium from the $10 billion that Walter paid just a year ago. Since then, the New York Times, Wall Street Journal and other outlets have reported that Walter is the focus of a federal probe into how he has handled some of his sports investments in recent years.

schema.headline: Jeanie Buss Seeks to Contest Sale of Los Angeles Lakers to Bob Iger and Josh Kushner: Report

title: David F. Sandberg to Direct Horror Movie ‘Mommy’s Home’ For Lionsgate
description:
David F. Sandberg has been tapped to direct a new psychological horror movie, “Mommy’s Home,” for Lionsgate. 

	From screenwriter James Morosini, “M
body:
David F. Sandberg has been tapped to direct a new psychological horror movie, “Mommy’s Home,” for Lionsgate. 

	From screenwriter James Morosini, “Mommy’s Home” follows “a young dad whose family life becomes terrifyingly unhinged when his cryogenically preserved mom is unfrozen and sent to live with him,” according to an official logline.

	Sandberg is probably best known for writing and directing his viral YouTube short turned horror feature “Lights Out.” He also helmed “Shazam!” and its 2023 sequel. His most directing credit was 2025’s “Until Dawn,” a big-screen adaptation of the popular horror video game for Sony. 
	

	Sandberg’s other upcoming projects include the sci-fi horror “Below” for Netflix and Atomic Monster as well as “A Little Slice of Hell” for Paramount. 


	Morosini usually works in front of the camera as an actor, recently starring in “It’s What’s Inside” for Netflix and Steve Pink’s sci-fi thriller “Terrestrial.” “Mommy’s Home” marks Morosini’s second feature credit as a screenwriter, after penning, directing and starring in the 2022 dark comedy “I Love My Dad.” 

	Producers for “Mommy’s Home” are Craig Flores, Dawn Olmstead and Anonymous Content. Sandberg and Lotta Losten also produce through their company Mångata. Executive producers include Nathan Kahane, Morosini, David Levine, Garrett Kemble and Ryan Schwartz. Scott O’Brien and Maria Ascanio are overseeing the project for Lionsgate. Dan Freedman negotiated the deal on behalf of the studio. 

	Sandberg is represented by CAA, Gotham Group, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman Wertheimer Mandelbaum Morris Bernstein Trattner Auerbach Hynick Jaime LeVine Sample & Klein. Morosini is represented by CAA and Eric Brooks and Matt Rosen at GGSSC.
	

	The InSneider was the first to report Sandberg’s involvement in “Mommy’s Home.”

schema.headline: David F. Sandberg to Direct Horror Movie ‘Mommy’s Home’ For Lionsgate

title: LISTEN: How Chris Carter Got a Second Shot at ‘The X-Files: I Want to Believe’ Film
description: On today’s episode of “Daily Variety” podcast, “The X-Files” creator Chris Carter explains to Variety’s Michael Schneider how he got the chance to d
body:
On today’s episode of “Daily Variety” podcast, “The X-Files” creator Chris Carter explains to Variety’s Michael Schneider how he got the chance to do a director’s cut of his 2008 “The X-Files: I Want to Believe” feature film. The new cut dubbed “The X-Files: I Want to Believe: Vrach Frankenshteyn” debuted Aug. 14 on Hulu and Disney+ outside the U.S.

	Carter points out that his preferred cut is actually shorter than the original release, which ran 144 minutes, per IMDB.
	

	“I always felt like people didn’t see the movie I intended to make,” Carter says, noting that 20th Century Studios executive Steve Asbell helped get the director’s cut project off the ground. “I asked him, ‘Have you ever thought about doing a director’s cut?’ And it was really just offhand. And he said, ‘Why? Would you like to do one?’ I said, ‘I’d love to do one.’ I can tell you, though, the reason for doing the director’s cut for me is not to put all the stuff that was taken out, but to put the right stuff in that was taken out.” 


	Carter discloses that for the original release in 2008, he was under a lot of pressure to ensure that the film would secure at PG-13 rating. 

	“When we showed them our first cut, the studio freaked out. They said, ‘This is torture porn. And you can’t do this for a PG-13 movie.’ So we cut it back and we satisfied them. And then we gave it to the motion picture folks, and they said, this isn’t a PG-13 movie. And we cut it back even further,” Carter says. “So the movie you’re seeing is, by and large, the movie that my partner in crime, [writer-producer] Frank Spotnitz, and I set out to make. And we always set out to make a very scary movie on a very limited budget, which is kind of the way we made ‘The X Files‘ TV series.”
	

	Carter makes a point of alerting “The X-Files” faithful to the independent horror film that he and his wife, writer Dori Carter, have recently completed in Vancouver. “Queens For a Day” revolves around “a very flawed person who has to go back in time and live her life through in someone else’s shoes,” Carter explains. He hopes to secure theatrical distribution for the film, which he directed, “in the next couple of months.”

	Listen to Daily Variety on iHeartPodcasts, Apple Podcasts, Variety’s YouTube Podcast channel, Amazon Music, Spotify and other podcast platforms.

schema.headline: LISTEN: How Chris Carter Got a Second Shot at ‘The X-Files: I Want to Believe’ Film

title: ‘Furious’ Star Steve Way on the Beauty of ‘Disabled Love’ and the Difficulty of Navigating Hollywood Without a Team: ‘I Want an Agency to Whore Me Out’
description: It’s uncommon to meet an actor bold enough to call Ari Emanuel, the executive chairman of WME Group and one of the most powerful people in Hollywood
body:
It’s uncommon to meet an actor bold enough to call Ari Emanuel, the executive chairman of WME Group and one of the most powerful people in Hollywood, a “prick” on the record.

	But it’s also uncommon to interview an actor as unfiltered as Steve Way.

	“I want an agency to whore me out,” he says. “Let’s make a ton of money together. Let’s change the world.” I joke that I’ll pass along his exact words to all the big companies. “Just get Ari on the phone,” he retorts. “Ari loves me. Except he won’t hire me.” That’s when Way mutters the p-word — under his breath for plausible deniability, but certainly still with the intention of being heard, smirking at the sound of my laughter. This is one of the last things he says to me before we wrap up our interview. A light blue Labubu that he’s clipped to his motorized wheelchair gives a wink as he rolls away.
	

	It’s impossible to fault Way, 35, for his ire. That’s partially because it’s well delivered — he’s got 15 years of stand-up comedy under his belt — but mostly because he works in an industry that seems determined to shut out people like him. Best known for his recurring role in Ramy Youssef’s self-titled dramedy series, and now giving an impeccable supporting performance in Hulu’s “Furious,” Way has no agent or manager. “And we know why,” he says, referring to his chair, his ventilator and the muscular dystrophy diagnosis he received at age 4.


	“I don’t have representation. And it’s frustrating, because I used to,” Way says. With his first agent, he got “nothing. Just nothing.” He signed with someone new, who later jumped to another agency and didn’t bring Way with him.
	



	

					Left to right: Ramy Youssef, Steve Way and Bella Hadid in “Ramy” Season 3.
									Courtesy of Hulu
	



	Way spent years wondering whether he’d be able to book a project without the support of Youssef, a close friend since childhood. Then, with “Furious,” he received something actors spend their whole careers dreaming of: a role written expressly for him.

	“Furious” is helmed by Elizabeth Meriwether, the writer-producer famed for creating “New Girl” and “The Dropout,” whom Way first met in 2025 when they appeared together on a WGA panel about on-screen depictions of caregiving. “I did the panel really high,” Way admits. He’d been on a stand-up tour as Youssef’s opener, and needed to relax after all the travel. “We’re going down the line talking about what we’re working on. Full resumes. And it got to me, and I was like, ‘I’m unemployed. If anyone wants to put me in their stuff, [I’ll join] gladly,’” Way recalls. Meriwether took his stoned comments to heart. “Two months later, I got an email from her people saying she wrote a part for me. That was it.”

	Way stars in the series as the love interest of the serial killer played by Lola Petticrew. To everyone else, Catherine is a sociopath. But to Alden, she’s simply a kindhearted in-home health aide who perhaps has a few secrets. As she feeds and bathes him with a gentle touch and a warm gaze, he returns the favor by giving her the benefit of the doubt about her shady comings and goings. Wanting to make the most of the time he has left after learning from doctors that his health has seriously worsened, Alden later proposes to Catherine with his late mother’s engagement ring, then begins abetting her crimes.

	There’s a profound sadness to the role, but “Furious” still makes plenty of room for the humor Way is known for. He applauds Meriwether for writing a disabled character who confronts his mortality but still has an identity beyond that, including a sense of humor. “When I read my first line — ‘You little slut!’ — I thought, ‘How does Liz know I would say that?” he says, smiling. “Right away, I knew that she would do the character justice.”

	When Danny (Scoot McNairy), a cop, suggests that Catherine is using him, Alden is resolute. “I don’t fucking care,” he says. “You think love is only when people do everything that you want them to do. That’s fucked up.”
	

	Way intimately understands that sentiment. “Everything is transactional. And as a disabled person, it’s very empowering to understand that. Caregiving is a two-way street. It has to be in order to work.” And the concept, in his eyes, isn’t exclusive to the relationship between disabled people and their aides. “Society has told a lot of lies about disabled people, mostly that we’re a burden. It’s not true. And to understand that is to accept that everyone, at some point in their life, receives care.”

	“When you take the subway, you don’t do that alone. Someone’s driving,” Way continues. “When you get DoorDash, that’s a level of care. So when Alden says that to Scoot’s character, in a way, he’s trying to radicalize him. Like, ‘You don’t get it, man.’” Smiling, he offers a phrase borrowed from his friend Danny Kurtzman, a fellow actor-producer with muscular dystrophy. “’Disabled love is the best love.’ Because of how intimate it is. How close you have to be,” he says.



	

					Lola Petticrew and Steve Way in “Furious.”
									Courtesy of Disney
	



	In Way’s opinion, “Alden and Catherine have the best relationship in the show: They had to get everything [uncomfortable] out of the way first and set up boundaries to make sure they could handle it. Like, ‘What’s your history with this person who’s keeping you alive? What do I do for them?’ It’s delicate, but there have to be boundaries, because it’s easy for any caregiver to get burnt out. That was really fun to figure out.”

	“Furious” was everything Way would have hoped for in terms of disability accommodations, thanks to the help of an on-set accessibility coordinator. “She made sure I was OK and advocated for me when I was really in the zone. Not once did I ever feel unsafe or not taken care of. It allowed me to just focus on the character. I wanted to feel the love and trust, to find our routines. Like, how would she would shower me? But also something as delicate as: How do we sit across from each other? How do we face each other lying down in a bed?”

	There were still moments when Way found himself pushing against his limits, physically. “There were some scenes that were uncomfortable — lying down for any extended period,” he says. But the discomfort was worth it to him. “I was locked in. Nothing else mattered; I just turned it off. The only thing that matters is the art that we’re operating here. That was my temporary. Yeah, the art. That’s it. The right thing for art, you know. That’s something that I realized no one can take away from me.
	

	Before “Furious,” Way wasn’t sure if his three-season run on “Ramy” had been enough to prove his talents to the industry. “I was scared people wouldn’t take me seriously. One time could be a fluke,” he says. “But twice? I’m pretty good at this.”



	

									Courtesy of Disney
	



	There’s still a long road ahead. Twice, Way has worked with a studio to develop a series he would create and star in himself, but both Apple TV and NBCUniversal ultimately passed. “It’s about the inner workings of a facility for disabled people,” he says. “We want to have a full disabled cast and show what it’s like to live in one building with not enough caregivers, with an administration who has no idea what they’re doing, in a country that doesn’t treat us the best. I think a lot of people will relate to it, and they’ll see the absurdity in our day-to-day.” 

	Slyly, he adds, “Shoutout Netflix!” — the streamer he hopes will be his next suitor.

	He’s gone through something similar with his stand-up comedy. He dreams of headlining his own tour. “It’s so hard to find accessible venues, but they’re out there. I gotta do my hour first, though,” he says. He’s already prepared — and taped — a full set he feels ready to show the world. He just hasn’t found a platform willing to help him turn it into a special. “Shoutout HBO!” he says.

	It’s par for the course at this point. “I’m numb to the noes,” Way says. “Because the noes have never stopped. And that’s OK. That’s just life; it’s no one’s fault. But it’s tough, because I have these big opportunities, and I don’t trust them.” With “Furious,” he tells me, he didn’t fully believe he’d get to be on TV again until his first day on set. “So when I hear that someone is interested in my show, I’ll take a meeting, but I don’t expect anything.”

	Still, he’s built more than he ever imagined for himself when he was younger. “I didn’t think I could have a career of any kind, because everyone told me I wouldn’t live long,” he says. “I almost died when I was 14, and I wasn’t supposed to live past 18. Then, when I was 25, my doctors told me I’m good. I was like, ‘Fuck! What now?’ I wasn’t good at anything besides telling jokes.” 

	So he keeps telling them. “The only thing that’s gonna stop me is my heart,” he says.
	

	And he’s also starting to enjoy the effects of the opportunity Meriwether gave him in “Furious.” For the first time, Way has a publicist, which he says has been “wonderful.”

	“It’s nice to respond to emails for once instead of initiating them, which is what I do every day,” Way says. Without a team behind him, the burden of seeking out the few roles available to disabled actors falls on him alone. “It’s tiring,” he says. “Espresso helps. Vodka helps. But I can’t run on that stuff forever.”

schema.headline: ‘Furious’ Star Steve Way on the Beauty of ‘Disabled Love’ and the Difficulty of Navigating Hollywood Without a Team: ‘I Want an Agency to Whore Me Out’

title: Michelle Rodriguez Remembers Hayden Panettiere After Co-Hosting World Music Awards: ‘Can’t Stand How Many Young People Are Leaving Us Lately’
description:
Michelle Rodriguez is sharing her memories of Hayden Panettiere after the “Scream 4” star died at age 36 on Sunday.

	Rodriguez and Panettiere co-ho
body:
Michelle Rodriguez is sharing her memories of Hayden Panettiere after the “Scream 4” star died at age 36 on Sunday.

	Rodriguez and Panettiere co-hosted the World Music Awards back in 2010. When asked what she remembers about Panettiere while walking the carpet at the 25th anniversary screening of “The Fast and the Furious,” Rodriguez told Variety, “Her curious spirit and how happy and joyous she is, because that’s her memory, right? I’ve got to tell you, man, I just can’t stand how many young people are leaving us lately. It’s disheartening, and it’s making me think, ‘What’s going on?’ It’s not normal.”
	

	She added, “I don’t want to speculate about anything, but it’s weird. Just in general, the amount and the volume of it since 2010 to now, it’s a lot.”


Michelle Rodriguez, who co-hosted the World Music Awards with Hayden Panettiere, remembers her as “happy and joyous” with a “curious spirit”:“I just can’t stand how many young people are leaving us lately. It’s disheartening. It’s not normal.”https://t.co/HCqrNMMe1z pic.twitter.com/sghig5ipiH— Variety (@Variety) August 18, 2026


	Many celebrities shared tributes for Panettiere online after news broke of her death. Viola Davis, who starred alongside Panettiere in the 2016 drama film “Custody,” shared a tribute on Instagram, writing, “I wish the world had more time with you because I had a burning curiosity about who you were becoming. I saw this beautiful Phoenix rising from the ashes. Your tests became your testimony, and your testimony became your legacy. You will be remembered. Rest well, Hayden. Sending healing prayers to your family, your daughter, and all who loved you. May they always speak your name.”

	Panettiere’s good friend and “One Tree Hill” star Bethany Joy Lenz likewise posted a remembrance on social media, along with photos of them together throughout the years. She wrote, “I knew the wild little blonde. Was she nine? Ten? I was eighteen. She ran through the Screen Gem studio hallways at 222 E44th St. laughing and playing games in between blocking and camera rehearsals. Long, unruly curls trailing behind her. She knew her lines and everyone else’s. Her intelligence was astonishing. She understood scenes and nuance and human struggle like no child I’d ever seen on camera. And she’d sit with you for a great conversation, then giggle and go play.”
	

	A cause of death has yet to be released. Panettiere’s father told ABC News on Sunday night, “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

schema.headline: Michelle Rodriguez Remembers Hayden Panettiere After Co-Hosting World Music Awards: ‘Can’t Stand How Many Young People Are Leaving Us Lately’

title: ‘Friday the 13th’ Prequel Series ‘Crystal Lake’ Is ‘Gory’ and ‘Gross’ With ‘Blood Everywhere,’ Says Star Linda Cardellini
description:
“Crystal Lake” star Linda Cardellini is teasing the upcoming “Friday the 13th” prequel television series.

	Cardellini stars in the Peacock series a
body:
“Crystal Lake” star Linda Cardellini is teasing the upcoming “Friday the 13th” prequel television series.

	Cardellini stars in the Peacock series as the franchise antagonist Pamela Voorhees. The show, premiering Oct. 15 on the streamer, follows Voorhees’ life prior to the events of the first “Friday the 13th” film. It also stars William Catlett as Levon Brooks, though exact character details remain under wraps. 


	“I remember one of my most fun moviegoing experiences was I saw ‘Freddy vs. Jason’ on the Universal City Walk, which is a giant movie theater, at the height of its popularity, and people were screaming at the screen and throwing things,” she told me Sunday at the HBO Max Emmy Nominee Celebration event in Hollywood.
	

	Does she predict the same for the new TV show? “This is a longer format so there’s a lot more you get to do in eight episodes,” Cardellini said. “It’s not necessarily like 90 minutes of pure horror. There’s a lot of story there. So maybe once in a while you’ll throw some things and scream.”

	And possibly cover your eyes.

	“It does get gory, yes, so much so that I wish sometimes they weren’t as practical as they were,” Cardellini said. “There’s a couple of gory moments on set that were very practical that were pretty gross. Blood everywhere at one point.”

Linda Cardellini teases the upcoming “Friday the 13th” prequel series, "Crystal Lake": “This is a longer format so there’s a lot more you get to do in eight episodes,” Cardellini said. “It’s not necessarily like 90 minutes of pure horror. There’s a lot of story there. So maybe… pic.twitter.com/NCB60HsEYq— Variety (@Variety) August 17, 2026


	Cardellini said most horror scripts she’s given are for characters who are running away from the killer. “Everything that I’ve ever read that was handed to me that was in that space was for the person who was being chased, not the person who was chasing everyone,” she said. “It was really fun this time to be on the other side of the knife.”
	

	Pamela first appeared in the original “Friday the 13th” movie in 1980 as Jason’s mother. She exacts revenge on people who she believed were responsible for Jason’s drowning in 1957 at Camp Crystal Lake.

	Cardellini attended the HBO Max Emmy event to celebrate her nomination for her work in “DTF St. Louis.”

title: Luigi Mangione's State Murder Trial Delayed After Federal Guilty Plea
description:
Luigi Mangione
                          State Murder Trial Pushed Back ...
body:
Luigi Mangione
                          State Murder Trial Pushed Back ...
                          As His Lawyers Try to Get Case Tossed
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Luigi Mangione will not go on trial for murder next month ... the start of his state proceedings have been delayed after his federal guilty plea last week.
      
    
            A judge in Manhattan has given state prosecutors until October 9 to respond to Luigi's request to dismiss the case ... thus pushing back the previous September 8 start date.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Luigi's legal team filed to dismiss the state case right after he pled guilty to federal stalking charges -- arguing that the guilty plea now bars the state case from moving forward under the federal Constitution and New York's double jeopardy law.
      

            Hit team also accused state and federal prosecutors of using him as a "pawn" in a coordinated push to punish him twice for the killing.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Luigi is still awaiting sentencing in the federal case ... he did not come to a plea agreement with prosecutors, so he's essentially at the judge's mercy. Federal sentencing guidelines recommend between 24 and 30 years.
      
    
            Not only did Luigi plead guilty to stalking ... but he also admitted he killed Brian Thompson -- a bombshell statement state prosecutors could use against him if the murder trial does happen.

title: Andrew Gillum Leaves Jail for Rehab After Alleged Positive Meth Test
description:
Ex-Florida Governor Nominee
                          Andrew Gillum Checks Into Rehab
body:
Ex-Florida Governor Nominee
                          Andrew Gillum Checks Into Rehab
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Andrew Gillum is swapping jail for rehab ... but the court will still be keeping close tabs on him.
      
    
            According to new legal documents obtained by TMZ, a judge ordered the former Florida gubernatorial candidate released from the Baldwin County Jail Friday ... so he could enter Cumberland Heights Treatment Center in Nashville.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Gillum must wear a GPS ankle monitor during his release ... and remain at the facility for at least 30 days, or however long it takes him to complete a drug and alcohol treatment program.
      

            The order says Gillum won't be allowed passes during intensive inpatient treatment. The judge says if he leaves without permission, he'll be considered an escapee and immediately arrested.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Gillum was taken back into custody earlier this month after prosecutors say he missed a random drug test and then tested positive for meth at a court appearance.
      
    
            His legal troubles began in July ... when Alabama cops said they pulled him over for driving erratically and found 3 grams of meth, 8 pre-rolled joints, cut straws, pipes and a bong.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Gillum is charged with felony meth possession and two misdemeanors.
      
    
            The order says if Gillum leaves the treatment center for any reason -- even after successfully completing inpatient treatment -- the judge must immediately be notified, and Gillum shall be returned to jail.
